history.summary: Shiv Temple at the village of Katalbodi, ~15 km west of Seoni, also called Matradham. Multiple travel sources state the Hindu guru Shankara Acharya constructed this temple here in 2003; CONFLICT (verify): one source (FreeDictionary/Seoni encyclopedia article) says it was built 'in honour of the birthplace of his mother', while another (ghoomophiro) describes Matradham as the guru's own birthplace - the exact claim varies by source. 'Shankara Acharya' here refers to a contemporary holder of the Shankaracharya title, not the 8th-century Adi Shankara (unverified). CSV TOWN FLAG: documented at Katalbodi village (Matradham), ~15 km west of Seoni town, not in Seoni town itself. Coordinates are approximate (railway-halt location used as proxy; village location approximate).

name: Matradham Mandir
town: Katalbodi village (Matradham), Seoni district (CSV town 'Seoni' is the nearby city, ~15 km away)
town_description: Katalbodi (Matradham) is a village about 15 km west of Seoni town, noted as a local religious site for the Shiv temple built by the guru Shankara Acharya in 2003. Seoni city is the headquarters of Seoni district in the Satpura range of Madhya Pradesh, famous as the setting of Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book'. The district also hosts the Pench Tiger Reserve.
